title: What is known about 1RB1RD_1LC0LE_1RA0LB_1RA1RF_0RA0RC_1RE---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RD_1LC0LE_1RA0LB_1RA1RF_0RA0RC_1RE---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The machine iterates a Collatz-like map: a block of m ones becomes, one phase later, a block of about 8m/3 ones, with a short prefix that acts as a second, nested counter. The cycle inside a phase is proved in Lean; the phase map is fitted case by case and agrees with direct simulation through 1.67·1010 steps. Iterated for 3,000 phases (about 102557 steps) it never meets a case that halts. Update, 13 November 2026: a search of all tails of at most 26 cells with the generic class map finds halting classes; the nearest needs 107 prescribed residues mod 3 in a row from the start of the run (observed, not proved). The machine is a cryptid.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 76,257 cells have been visited and 46,382 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: The cycle of a phase
claims.text: For all x, y and any tape L to the left, L 1^(x+3) (01)^y 1 D>0 reaches L 1^x (01)^(y+4) 1 D>0 in 6y + 39 steps.

claims.title: The phase map, checked against the simulator
claims.text: From the phase start Q 0 1^m (01)^5 1 D>0 with m = 3k + r, the next phase start is Q' 0 1^(8k+c) (01)^5 1 D>0 with Q' and c fixed by (Q, r), and a step count 12k² + Bk + C. Fitted on four block sizes per case; the predicted start steps of phases 1 to 9 (3,291 ... 16,707,143,908) equal those of the direct C simulation.

claims.title: 3,000 phases without a halting case
claims.text: The fitted map, iterated from blank tape for 3,000 phases (to about 10<sup>2557</sup> steps), meets 68 (prefix, remainder) cases, none of which halts; the 120 prefixes nearest the empty one (breadth first) have no halting case either.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.505).

claims.title: Rounds between end events, by remainder class
claims.text: Sample the run whenever the head is in state D reading 1 with only 0s to its right. Read leftwards from the head, the tape is then A U^m B: one long periodic block between two short context words. For each class (A, U, B, m mod 3) the next sample is simulated for six values of m and extended as an affine map of m (with a cubic step count). Along the direct run from blank tape to 3·109 steps (10 events) the class map predicts the next event in all 7 rounds it applies to. This is an extrapolation checked by computation, not a proof.

claims.title: 185,703 rounds of the class map without a halt
claims.text: Iterated with exact integers from the event at step 3,238 of the run (A = (empty), U = 1, m = 109, B = 0 16): 185,703 rounds without meeting a halting class; m then has 262,784 bits (about 10158,210 steps of the machine). 119 distinct contexts occur, the longest of 28 cells.

claims.title: No halting class among 5,000 contexts
claims.text: Breadth first from the starting context, with every remainder at every context (whether or not the numbers can really produce that sequence of remainders, and only for m large compared with the contexts): 5,000 contexts expanded, 5,440 found, to depth 43. None of them halts; the search is not complete (the set of contexts keeps growing), and it says nothing about a halt that needs a context as long as the block itself.

claims.title: A halting class is reachable, 107 rounds away
claims.text: The same search restricted to contexts of at most 26 cells runs to the end: 10,061 contexts (1,649 longer ones are reached but not expanded), and 5 of their classes halt. The nearest is 107 rounds from the starting context: after the remainders 1 22 1 2 12 2 13 22 1 22 12 22 1 2 12 22 1 22 13 22 1 22 1 22 12 22 13 22 1 2 13 22 1 22 12 22 1 2 12 22 1 22 13 22 1 22 1 22 12 22 1 2 12 22 1 22 13 22 1 22 1 2 (mod 3) the tail is 01011011, and with m ≡ 1 (mod 3) the machine halts before the next event (all six simulated values of m halt). So, granted the class map, a halt is possible, but only through one prescribed sequence of 107 remainders or a longer one; with remainders like fair dice that is one chance in 3107 per try. The orbit computed has not come near it.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Granted the class map (observed, not proved), it halts exactly if the orbit ever reaches a halting class; the nearest known one needs 107 prescribed remainders mod 3 in a row. A Collatz-like question about one orbit: a cryptid.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine plays a game much like the 3n+1 problem: a block of m ones is ground down three at a time, and then rebuilt as a block of about 8m/3 ones, with the details set by the remainder of m divided by 3. This page runs the real machine in your browser and explains the game.

facts.text: One cycle of a phase, proved in Lean for all sizes.
Phase to phase, a Collatz-like map on the block size and a short prefix; exact against the simulator through 1.67·10<sup>10</sup> steps.
3,000 phases of the fitted map without reaching a halting case.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.

sections.heading: Some remainder classes halt, 107 rounds away
html: A generic test used on the whole family: sample the run whenever the head is in state D reading 1 with only 0s to its right. Read leftwards from the head, the tape is then A Um B, one long periodic block between two short context words A and B. The round to the next sample is computed class by class: for a class (A, U, B, m mod 3) six values of m are simulated, and when they agree the round is taken to be an affine map of m. Against the direct run to 3·109 steps the class map is right in all 7 rounds it applies to. It is an observed law, not a proved one.

The orbit. Iterated with exact integers from the event at step 3,238 of the run (A = (empty), U = 1, m = 109, B = 0 16): 185,703 rounds without meeting a halting class; m then has 262,784 bits (about 10158,210 steps of the machine). 119 distinct contexts occur, the longest of 28 cells.

Can any class halt? Breadth first from the starting context, with every remainder at every context (whether or not the numbers can really produce that sequence of remainders, and only for m large compared with the contexts): 5,000 contexts expanded, 5,440 found, to depth 43. None of them halts; the search is not complete (the set of contexts keeps growing), and it says nothing about a halt that needs a context as long as the block itself.

A halt is reachable. The same search restricted to contexts of at most 26 cells runs to the end: 10,061 contexts (1,649 longer ones are reached but not expanded), and 5 of their classes halt. The nearest is 107 rounds from the starting context: after the remainders 1 22 1 2 12 2 13 22 1 22 12 22 1 2 12 22 1 22 13 22 1 22 1 22 12 22 13 22 1 2 13 22 1 22 12 22 1 2 12 22 1 22 13 22 1 22 1 22 12 22 1 2 12 22 1 22 13 22 1 22 1 2 (mod 3) the tail is 01011011, and with m ≡ 1 (mod 3) the machine halts before the next event (all six simulated values of m halt). So, granted the class map, a halt is possible, but only through one prescribed sequence of 107 remainders or a longer one; with remainders like fair dice that is one chance in 3107 per try. The orbit computed has not come near it.
That makes the machine a cryptid: whether it halts is a question about one orbit of a Collatz-like map, and nothing known decides it.

sections.heading: A block of ones turning into pairs
html: Every time the head reaches the right end of the tape in state D, the tape reads Q 0 1x (01)y 1 D>0: a short prefix Q, a solid block of x ones, and a run of y pairs 01. The head walks left over the pairs, eats three ones off the end of the block, and walks back writing four new pairs:
1x+3 (01)y 1 D>0  →  1x (01)y+4 1 D>0   (6y + 39 steps)

This one cycle is proved in Lean for all x, y (cycle, lean/Cycle.lean). A phase is the run of cycles from a full block down to fewer than three ones: a block of m = 3k + r ones lasts k cycles and leaves about 4k pairs.

sections.heading: Phases: a Collatz-like map that multiplies by 8/3
html: When fewer than three ones are left (r = m mod 3 of them), the head runs into the prefix, rebuilds it, and turns the long run of pairs back into a solid block: about two ones per pair, so the next block is m' = 8k + c, roughly 8m/3. The constant c and the new prefix depend only on the old prefix and on r. For the empty prefix:

m mod 3next prefixnext block m'
0empty8k + 12
1empty8k + 14
2168k + 8

So the machine is iterating a map like the famous 3n+1 problem: what happens next depends on a remainder, and the numbers grow by a factor of 8/3 per phase. sections.heading: The prefix is a smaller copy of the same machine
html: The prefix Q has the same shape as the main tape, 1a (01)b. A phase ending with remainder 2 pushes work into it (the empty prefix becomes 16, then 13(01)2, ...: three ones become two pairs, just like a cycle); remainder 0 takes one pair off; remainder 1 usually runs the prefix's own little phase and empties it. Some cases nest a third level (16 0 14, ...). Over 3,000 phases the prefix was empty 62% of the time and never longer than about 20 cells.

The halting transition is F reading a 1, reached only as D>1 1. In all 68 (prefix, remainder) cases met in 3,000 phases, and in the 120 prefixes reached breadth first from the empty one, the phase ends in a new phase start: no case halts.

sections.heading: What is proved and what is not
html: • Proved (kernel): the halting configurations, no halt in the first 10,000 steps (107 with native_decide), and the cycle rule for all sizes.

• Computed: the phase map, fitted case by case on small blocks (four sizes each, step count included) and checked against the direct simulation step for step through phase 9 (1.67·1010 steps). Iterated 3,000 phases (about 102557 steps) it never reaches a case that halts.

• Open: each case of the map is fitted, not proved, and the prefix can in principle grow without bound (a long run of remainder-2 phases), so there are infinitely many cases. A proof of non-halting would need every case, by induction on the prefix, and an argument that the run never meets a halting one.

Heuristic. If the remainders behave like fair random digits, the prefix behaves like a walk pushed back towards empty, and a halting case, if one exists at all, would have to be reached through an unusually deep prefix. No such case is known; the map so far gives no sign that it halts.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB0RE_1LC0RA_1LA1LD_1LC1LF_0LC0LB_1LE---: rename A→C, B→A, C→B, D→D, E→E, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state B, in a mirror
  • 1RB0LC_1RC1RE_1LA0LD_0RB0RA_1RB1RF_1RD---: rename A→B, B→C, C→A, D→E, E→D, F→F; it is this table started in state C

summary: A block of ones is turned into 01 pairs three at a time; phase to phase the block grows like m -> 8m/3 + c, with c and a nested prefix counter set by m mod 3 (Collatz-like; a halting case is 107 prescribed remainders away, observed; a cryptid).
